# PyPI corpus for Health Score debugging. Not a real project.
# See qa/health-score-instruction.md; scan with --cutoff-date=2026-08-15 for reproducibility.
#
# Every pin is deliberate. The goal is spread across the model's inputs, not a realistic project:
# a corpus where every package sits on `latest` collapses the exposure window onto the flat
# ECOSYSTEM_FIX_PRIOR (60.0d on PyPI) and makes that entire term invisible.
#
# requirements.txt rather than pyproject.toml because a bare pyproject with no lockfile is not
# detected (api_uv/api_pip both require one). The cost is that pip-classic reports
# optional_dependencies={}, so every package here is tier="runtime" - the dev tier and the
# install-execution multiplier are exercised by the npm fixture instead.

# abandoned, archived upstream, unresolved CVEs, installed == latest.
# The W-floor reference case: zero upgrade distance, so W is exactly 60.0d and no maintenance
# signal can move it (HEALTH_SCORE_PLAN.md H0/H1).
pycrypto==2.6.1

# CVE with a low EPSS and an overdue fix: the negligence-bump reference case (H7).
click==8.1.3

# CVE plus minor lag - EPSS hazard accruing over a window that is not on the floor.
requests==2.28.1

# Several CVEs and a major lag: hazard summation across CVEs, largest upgrade distance.
urllib3==1.26.5

# Critical CVE with a fix available -> Gate blocks regardless of the probability chain.
pyyaml==5.4.1

# CVE plus moderate lag; a second multi-release-lag data point.
jinja2==3.0.0

# Mature, no CVE at this pin: the P_vuln == 0.0 control. Without it the corpus cannot show
# whether a clean package is distinguishable from a vulnerable one.
numpy==1.26.4
